candidates.title: Maersk lowers Thamesport EFS and holds Felixstowe charge
candidates.excerpt: Maersk has announced the Emergency Fuel Surcharge levels applicable to laden import containers moving through the Port of Felixstowe and London Thamesport during November and December 2026. At Felixstowe, the surcharge remains unchanged at £4.44 per laden import container for both months. The new rates will cover shipments to the west and east coasts of South America, as well as the west and east coasts of Central America. The Caribbean and Mexico are also included. The increase applies to dry containers, refrigerated cargo, out-of-gauge shipments and paying empty containers. The carrier has specified a single amount per container rather than separate charges based on TEU capacity. The adjustment will take effect according to the cargo loading date. Seven of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They included motor vehicles and parts, up 1,443 carloads, to 15,283; metallic ores and metals, up 1,215 carloads, to 20,274; and forest products, up 774 carloads, to 8,401. Commodity groups that posted decreases compared with the same week in 2025 were coal, down 698 carloads, to 56,997; grain, down 589 carloads, to 23,708; and nonmetallic minerals, down 561 carloads, to 32,376. Seven of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. candidates.title: Schneider to shift eastern rail business to Norfolk Southern from CSX
candidates.excerpt: Schneider will make Norfolk Southern its primary eastern rail provider under an agreement announced Oct. 29 aimed at expanding domestic intermodal capacity and giving shippers more options to move freight across the eastern United States. The agreement, effective in November, shifts Schneider’s NYSE: SNDR) company-owned equipment, drivers and logistics operations away from CSX (NASDAQ: CSX) and pairs it with Norfolk Southern’s 22-state intermodal network. The companies said the partnership would expand market access, increase capacity flexibility and help attract freight now moving by truck. “As we transition our primary eastern rail provider to Norfolk Southern, we’ll expand access to key markets, increase network flexibility and create new opportunities to better serve our customers,” said Michael Baumgardt, Schneider’s executive vice president of intermodal and logistics, in a release. Weekly intermodal volume, which includes containers and trailers, rose 11.3%, while carload traffic increased 3.6%. Both measures grew faster than their respective year-to-date rates. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded year-over-year increases. Petroleum and petroleum products led percentage growth, rising 15.4%, followed by motor vehicles and parts at 15.3%. Forest products increased 11.7%, and metallic ores and metals gained 11.6%. Farm products excluding grain, and food fell 3.7%, while grain posted a rare decline at 1.4%. For the first 42 weeks of 2026, combined U.S. rail traffic increased 3.8% from the same period in 2025. Carloads rose 2.7%, while intermodal traffic was better by 4.7%. Revenue declined 22% to $591 million from $759.5 million. Excluding facility-rationalization costs, core earnings were 39 cents a share. The charges reduced quarterly earnings by 12 cents a share after tax and non-controlling interests.
